`final class UIBridgeRegistry`<br/>
**Extends:** [`BridgeRegistry<UIBridge>`](/reference/bridges/bridgeregistry/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.bridge.ui` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [UIBridgeRegistry.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/bridge/ui/UIBridgeRegistry.java)

The registry of UI bridges, which runs the frame of each one and routes the input between them.

## Description

`BridgeHandler.UI` is the only instance.
[`Backend.frame`](/reference/backends/backend/#Backend-method-frame) calls `frame()`, and the input forwarders of the backends call the input methods; you call them yourself only when you forward the input of a host by hand.
Each input method returns `true` when JOID consumed the event, which should then not reach the rest of your application.

<a id="UIBridgeRegistry-method-charTyped"></a>

### charTyped

`boolean charTyped(int codepoint)` 

Sends a typed Unicode code point to the bridges from the highest priority down, until one consumes it.

<a id="UIBridgeRegistry-method-keyPressed"></a>

### keyPressed

`boolean keyPressed(Key physicalKey, Key key)` 

Records the press in the key state, with the physical key and the key of the layout, then sends it to the bridges from the highest priority down, until one consumes it.
Key repeats come from JOID itself: send only the first press.

<a id="UIBridgeRegistry-method-keyReleased"></a>

### keyReleased

`boolean keyReleased(Key physicalKey)` 

Records the release in the key state and sends it to every bridge; returns `true` when the press of that key was consumed, so that the host hides its release too.

<a id="UIBridgeRegistry-method-isKeyConsumed"></a>

### isKeyConsumed

`boolean isKeyConsumed(Key physicalKey)` 

If `true`, a bridge consumed the last press of that physical key.

<a id="UIBridgeRegistry-method-getKeyState"></a>

### getKeyState

`KeyState getKeyState()` 

Returns the state of the held keys, which [`Key.isDown`](/reference/input/key/#Key-method-isDown) reads for the keys that depend on the layout.

<a id="UIBridgeRegistry-method-get"></a>

### get

`IUIBridge get(UI ui)` 

Returns the bridge that holds the UI when it is open, otherwise the bridge of highest priority that can handle it, or `null`.

`IUIBridge get(Class<? extends UI> clazz)` 

Returns the bridge of highest priority that can handle UIs of that class, or `null`.

<a id="UIBridgeRegistry-method-frame"></a>

### frame

`void frame()` 

Runs one frame: when the window size changed and is not zero, it resizes the screen and lays every UI out again; then it runs `fireFrame()`, updates every bridge, begins the frame of the render bridge, lets the bridge of lowest priority draw the background, draws every bridge from the lowest priority to the highest, and ends the frame.

<a id="UIBridgeRegistry-method-fireFrame"></a>

### fireFrame

`void fireFrame()` 

Runs the tasks queued by other threads on every [`FrameThreadBridge`](/reference/bridges/framethreadbridge/), then the tasks given to `onFrame`; `frame()` calls it.
